advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether transport-carrying dataclass fields (e.g. `BatchApplyContext.client: Any`) are in scope for the cc77 blindness guard; if so, extend detection to `ast.AnnAssign` class fields, otherwise document the parameter-only scope explicitly.
evidence: `_port_params` only walks `if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)` and reads `node.args`, so class-level `ast.AnnAssign` fields are never examined
apply_handlers.py:78: `    client: Any` inside `@dataclass class BatchApplyContext`, whose docstring (apply_handlers.py:70) says 'Handlers read the resolved transport (`client`)'
outbound_differ.py:261: `    client: Any = None` is a dataclass field carrying the transport
Module docstring lists `client: Any` (example 2) as one of the three spellings this file is meant to fail on, but a field spelling escapes because only parameters are checked
advisory.finding: The guard only inspects function/method PARAMETERS (`ast.arg` nodes) and therefore does not catch transport-carrying dataclass FIELDS annotated `Any`, even though those are the same blind-port pattern the module's own docstring example #2 warns about. `apply_handlers.py:78` (`client: Any` on `BatchApplyContext`, documented as 'the resolved transport') and `outbound_differ.py:261` (`client: Any = None`) are real core-module transport references that stay `Any` and are invisible to this test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Collapse the two `next(...)` lookups in `test_the_only_deliberate_any_is_the_runtime_guard_itself` into a single comprehension that yields the `arg` node directly.
evidence: Line 167-169: `guard = next(f for f, p, a in _port_params(tree) if f == "assert_transport_conforms" and p == "transport")` binds `guard` to the string `'assert_transport_conforms'`

Line 170: `arg = next(a for f, p, a in _port_params(tree) if f == guard and p == "transport")` then re-searches for the same `(f, p)` pair to obtain the `arg` node that was already available in the first comprehension
advisory.finding: In `test_the_only_deliberate_any_is_the_runtime_guard_itself`, the `guard` variable is bound to the function-NAME string via `next(f for f, p, a in ... if f == 'assert_transport_conforms' ...)`, then immediately re-used in a second `next(a for f, p, a in ... if f == guard ...)`. Since `guard` just equals the literal `'assert_transport_conforms'`, the first comprehension is redundant scaffolding that reads as if it were computing something.
advisory.suggested_fix:
arg = next(a for f, p, a in _port_params(tree) if f == "assert_transport_conforms" and p == "transport")
assert arg.annotation is not None
assert "Any" in _annotation_names(arg.annotation)
